title: Try it locally
summary: Run the local trial: a fictional company, a local CISO Assistant, your coding agent and every collector against built-in dev servers. No account, key or cloud needed.

steps.title: The scene: a small business and its GRC platform
narration: Welcome to Evidence Hound.
In this tutorial you try it on your own machine, with a fictional company called Example Pty Ltd.
Example Pty Ltd runs CISO Assistant and Evidence Hound on one private cloud VM, its GRC platform.
The office reaches it over a VPN through a Sophos firewall, and staff sign in with Microsoft 365.
The GRC team audits each system against the Essential Eight, maturity level two.
Everything you are about to run reads fictional tenants on your machine, so nothing leaves it.

panel.title: Example Pty Ltd
lines: GRC-PLATFORM: CISO Assistant and Evidence Hound on one OCI VM, no public address
OFFICE-FIREWALL: a Sophos XGS 88W managed in Sophos Central
Microsoft 365 for every account and laptop
Essential Eight, maturity level 2, audited by quarter

steps.title: Start the trial
narration: Open this repository in its dev container, which has Docker and everything else the trial needs.
Then run make trial.
It checks Docker, finds or starts a local CISO Assistant, and builds the hound runner image from your checkout.
The first build takes a while. Every later run skips the steps it has finished.
Your turn: type the command that starts the trial.

steps.title: The organisation, with hound init
narration: First, hound init asks about the organisation.
Press Enter to take each default: Example Pty Ltd, maturity level two, audited by quarter.
It writes the compliance repo: the config, the scope and the Essential Eight mapping.
Then hound plans what it would change in CISO Assistant, and shows you before it applies anything.

steps.title: Bring in your coding agent
narration: From here your coding agent does the reading and drafting, and you approve.
hound agent setup writes the skills and agent files for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot into the trial repo.
Start your agent in a second terminal, in the trial repo, and keep it open.
The trial has already put fictional supplier notes in the inbox folder, for your agent to read.

steps.title: Third parties: the agent drafts, you approve
narration: The trial prints what to ask your agent at each stage.
First the third parties: Oracle for hosting, Sophos for the firewall, and the two open-source projects.
The agent drafts each one with hound supplier draft, giving every risk level a reason.
Then you run hound approve in your own terminal, and answer each draft yes or no.
A system is only registered once its supplier is approved.

terminal.command: hound supplier draft --system GRC-PLATFORM --ref SUP-ORACLE --name "Oracle Cloud Infrastructure" --solution-ref SOL-OCI-HOSTING --solution-name "OCI compute, networking and storage" --contract-ref CTR-OCI-2026 --contract-name "OCI pay-as-you-go 2026" --level "dependency=3:The GRC platform runs only on it; moving it is a planned project." --kind vendor

steps.title: Each system gets its own audit
narration: Next, each system.
The agent starts an onboarding session for the GRC platform, then decides every Essential Eight requirement, one at a time.
Each decision says how the requirement is met: by an API check, by manual evidence, by another system, or not applicable, with its reasoning.
You approve the decisions, and hound writes the system's own audit.
The firewall gets the same treatment, so each system's gaps show on their own.

terminal.command: hound onboard GRC-PLATFORM pending --json --repo . --group 1 --group 2 --owner it@example.com --product "GRC platform" --solution SOL-OCI-HOSTING

steps.title: Collectors gather the evidence
narration: Now the evidence.
The trial starts dev servers that answer like Sophos Central, Microsoft 365 and an infrastructure pipeline, all on your machine.
It adds a collector for each, runs it dry first, then publishes the results to the right audit.
Then it breaks something on purpose, such as unsupported firewall firmware, and runs again, so you can watch the result turn to non-compliant in CISO Assistant.

steps.title: Read each audit honestly
narration: Last, the trial reads each audit's compliance figure the way CISO Assistant computes it.
A row with no evidence yet is sent as non-compliant, never left blank, so an audit cannot read one hundred percent by leaving rows out.
That is your starting point: the gaps you see are real, and each one names what it still needs.

terminal.output:
== 16. What CISO Assistant reads for each audit ==
EX-E8-Q2-2027FY: CISO Assistant reads 14% (16 compliant, 0 partially compliant, 91 non-compliant of which 81 have no evidence yet; it leaves out 0 not applicable and 0 not assessed).
A row with no evidence counts against the figure until its evidence arrives.

choice.question: An audit has three passing checks and every manual row not assessed. What should it read?

options.feedback: That is what leaving rows out would show. hound sends a row with no evidence as non-compliant so it cannot happen.

options.text: A low figure, because rows with no evidence count against it.
options.feedback: No evidence is not compliance. The figure rises as evidence arrives.
